currentState.summary: RayX has rayx_runtime_theming_dtcg under crates/rayx, but that crate resolves DTCG assets into RayX RuntimeTheme, GlobalTokens, and component token overrides. The reusable pieces need to become an independent dtcg_runtime crate with a companion derive crate, while RayX-specific AssetService, gpux conversion, AppBuilder, and RuntimeTheme deletion move to the dependent rayx_dtcg epic.

decisions.title: Build a reusable I/O-free runtime crate
decisions.decision: Create crates/rayx/dtcg_runtime and crates/rayx/dtcg_runtime_derive. dtcg_runtime owns ResourceId, DocumentRequest, Resolution<T>, DtcgRuntime, semantic model, cache, error types, limits, projection traits, TypeRegistry, and public derive re-exports. dtcg_runtime_derive emits only generic projection metadata and contains no RayX knowledge.
decisions.rationale: This isolates the design-token engine from RayX application policy and allows other UI libraries to use the same resolver with their own loading and conversion layers.
controlFlow: Ready returns typed output; Missing returns document requests.
dataFlow: JSON text -> catalog snapshot -> semantic token graph -> optional projection -> caller-owned output.
failureHandling: Malformed input and invalid resource IDs return structured errors without partial batch mutation.
Missing documents are returned as data rather than loaded internally.
concurrencyAndTransactions: Catalog mutation increments a revision and clears caches.
Resolution reads one immutable catalog revision.
compatibilityAndMigration: No legacy RuntimeTheme, GlobalTokens, or ComponentTokenStore names are exported.
The dependent rayx_dtcg epic consumes the stable public API after this epic checkpoints.
observability: Errors and optional traces include catalog revision, resource ID, JSON pointer, token path, context, and provenance without logging full documents.
securityAndPrivacy: The runtime contains no ambient I/O authority and treats identifiers as opaque logical IDs.

decisions.title: Resolve by token-path operations
decisions.decision: Normalize DTCG token documents into ordered operations over TokenPath -> RawToken plus group metadata. Walk resolutionOrder and source arrays in declaration order, apply whole-token replacement at matching token paths, then resolve effective types and aliases across the complete active graph before projection.
decisions.rationale: DTCG overlay semantics operate on token identities rather than arbitrary JSON object fields. A semantic intermediate prevents accidental deep merge and keeps aliases consistent with the final selected context.
dataFlow: DTCG node + source provenance -> RawToken -> winning token map -> ResolvedToken -> ResolvedGroup.
failureHandling: Alias and reference walkers keep visited stacks and return full cycle chains.
Composite overrides validate as complete replacement values.
concurrencyAndTransactions: Stable vectors and ordered maps prevent iteration nondeterminism.
compatibilityAndMigration: Legacy override compiler merge behavior is not reused.
observability: Test-only operation traces expose ordered operations and winning-token provenance.
securityAndPrivacy: Depth and token-count limits apply before semantic expansion.

decisions.title: Use explicit lazy catalog APIs
decisions.decision: DtcgRuntime stores Arc<str> documents by fragment-free ResourceId. from_json and provide_json accept logical identifiers plus JSON text. Relative references canonicalize against referenced_from. resolve returns Ready or Missing. provide_requested_json validates request identity, provide_json_batch is atomic, and validate_complete is a separate traversal that can inspect inactive contexts.
decisions.rationale: This supports AssetService, in-memory tests, library-owned loaders, HTTP clients, and preloaded string catalogs without embedding a loader.
controlFlow: Caller resolves again until Ready or Error.
dataFlow: Original $ref + parent ResourceId -> canonical ResourceId + fragment.
DocumentRequest -> external loader -> JSON string -> catalog revision.
failureHandling: Invalid ResourceId, traversal, fragment syntax, JSON, or request mismatch leaves catalog unchanged.
concurrencyAndTransactions: Catalog mutation increments u64 revision and invalidates caches.
compatibilityAndMigration: Path-oriented RayX call sites move to logical IDs in the dependent RayX epic.
observability: Requests retain original and canonical references.
securityAndPrivacy: Canonicalization rejects traversal above the logical root and malformed pointer escaping.

decisions.title: Generate strict projected views
decisions.decision: DtcgTokens derive generates static field schema and projection code. Nested DtcgTokens fields consume groups; leaves use TypeRegistry by (target TypeId, effective DTCG type). Projection rejects missing requested fields and invalid requested aliases while tolerating additional active tokens. #[dtcg(rest)] collects registered unclaimed groups without changing the JSON hierarchy.
decisions.rationale: Serde cannot select converters by both DTCG semantic type and target foreign Rust type. Projection metadata keeps user structs simple while preserving precise errors.
controlFlow: Projection ignores unclaimed tokens unless rest owns them.
Projection constructs T only after every requested field succeeds.
dataFlow: ResolvedToken + ProjectionContext -> converter -> Box<dyn Any> -> checked downcast -> field.
Unprojected token -> alias target for projected token.
failureHandling: Every error includes Rust field path, token path, effective DTCG type, expected Rust type, and source resource.
Converter panic policy is explicit and tested.
concurrencyAndTransactions: Registry is frozen into an immutable generation for cache keys.
compatibilityAndMigration: RayX-specific converters are not introduced here.
observability: Projection schema dump lists Rust field path, DTCG path, target type, and expected DTCG type.
securityAndPrivacy: Converters receive resolved values rather than raw documents.
validation: Narrow AppTheme over wider graph test.

decisions.title: Expose a test-suite visual diagnostics route
decisions.decision: Add a generic DTCG runtime page under apps/test_suite and a matching tools-node/test_suite spec. The page embeds small DTCG JSON strings, calls only public dtcg_runtime APIs, displays resolved token rows, contexts, missing document requests, projection output, provenance, and structured errors, and includes a fixture where spacing is internal but still used by a projected component-like token.
decisions.rationale: The runtime is generic, but developers need a fast visual playground to inspect resolver behavior, especially overlay and alias cases that are hard to reason about from unit test output alone.
controlFlow: Controls select contexts or invalid scenario.
Page renders Ready, Missing, or Error state.
dataFlow: Embedded JSON -> dtcg_runtime -> display rows -> Playwright assertions.
failureHandling: Invalid fixture renders a visible diagnostic panel rather than panicking.
concurrencyAndTransactions: Route state changes synchronously from user controls; no loader thread is introduced.
compatibilityAndMigration: The route remains a consumer of dtcg_runtime and does not create RayX DTCG policy.
observability: The page exposes resource IDs, token paths, effective types, provenance, and fingerprints.
securityAndPrivacy: Fixture document bodies are not dumped wholesale.
validation: Headed WASM/WebGPU test asserts visible resolved values, Missing requests, context switch, internal alias behavior, and diagnostics.

alternatives.alternative: Keep RayX AssetService integration inside dtcg_runtime
advantages: Provides one high-level load-and-resolve call for RayX applications.
disadvantages: Introduces RayX I/O authority and prevents independent UI-library adoption.
alternatives.reasonRejected: It makes the reusable resolver depend on RayX I/O and prevents other UI libraries from using already-loaded strings.

alternatives.alternative: Deserialize several Rust structs and merge them
advantages: Uses familiar Serde derives and ordinary Rust values.
disadvantages: Cannot express ordered token replacement, aliases after overlay, or reference-only namespaces correctly.
alternatives.reasonRejected: Serde does not define DTCG overlay semantics and aliases must resolve before typed structs exist.

alternatives.alternative: Validate every active DTCG token during ordinary projection
advantages: Reports every latent invalid token during each projection.
disadvantages: Rejects valid internal tokens that the requested Rust view intentionally does not expose.
alternatives.reasonRejected: It rejects valid reference-only namespaces that are intentionally absent from the public Rust target.
